title: 4. Ethernet
content: The dominant wired and wireless LAN technology. It is the first widely used LAN technology. It uses the *Manchester encoding scheme*. **Carrier Sense**: Wait for link to be idle. If the channel is idle, start transmitting. Otherwise, wait until idle. **Collision Detection**: Listen while transmitting. If a collision is detected, abort the transmission and send a jam signal. - *Random Access:* Exponential back-off. After a collision, wait a random amount of time before trying again. Uses **CSMA/CD** (Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Detection). This basically just means that Ethernet is a set of nodes that send and receive frames over a shared link where each node can: - distinguish between a busy and idle link - listen as it transmits so it can tell when a frame it transmits collides with some other frame - **Ethernet segment:** A coaxial cable of up to 500 m - Hosts connect to a segment by tapping into it - **Transceiver:** attached directly to the tap. It detects when the line is idle and drives signal when the host is transmitting. - Receives incoming signal. - Connected to an Ethernet adapter that is plugged into the host - **Adapter**: Implements the protocol **Repeater**: A device that forwards digital signals. Multiple segments are joined together by repeaters. Any signal placed on the Ethernet by a host is broadcast over the entire network. - Signal is propagated in both directions. - Repeaters forward the signal on all outgoing segments. - Terminators attached to the end of each segment absorb the signal ### Limitations Latency depends on the physical length of link. If a collision is detected, the sender won't see it for $2 \times \text{ link latency}$ - *Maximum wire length is 2500 meters* - *Maximum length of the packet is 512 bits (64 bytes)* ## Access Protocol for Ethernet Algorithm is called Ethernet's **Media Access Control (MAC)**. - It is implemented in Hardware on the network adaptor. #### Frame format - Preamble (64 bit): Allows the receiver to synchronize with the signal - Host and Destination Address (48 bit each) - Packet Type (16 bit) - Data (up to 1500 bytes) - Frame must contain at least **46 bytes** of data so that it is long enough to detect collision - CTC (32 bit) - Checked at receiver. Frame is dropped if an error is detected. - *No error correction just error detection.* ## Addresses Each host on Ethernet has a unique Ethernet address (belonging to an adaptor not host). **Unicast Address**: Identifies one specific L2 interface. **Broadcast Address**: A special address consisting of all 1s is sent to everyone up to the host. **Multicast Address**: Like broadcast but we can program an adaptor to indicate what group of hosts should receive frames. ## Transmission Algorithm ### TODO: Missing Notes # Physical Layer ## Repeaters There is a distance limitation in LAN because electrical signal becomes weaker as it travels. **Repeaters** join LANs together. They are an analog electronic device that monitors electrical signals and transmits an amplified copy. ## Hubs Joins multiple input lines electrically. It is designed to hold multiple line cards. Do not necessarily amplify the signal. ### Limitations of Hubs & Repeaters 1. There becomes one large collision domain because every bit is sent everywhere 2. Cannot support multiple LAN technologies 3. A limit on maximum nodes and distances ## Bridges Connects two or more LANs at link layer. - Extracts destination address from the frame - Looks up the destination in a table - Forwards the frame to the appropriate LAN segment Each segment becomes its own collision domain A device that offers several advantages over hubs and repeaters (such as applying CS and CD) with the drawback of being more expensive machines that have a delay in forwarding frames (because they need to learn where to forward frames (*routing table*)) ## Switches Like a bridge but for hosts not LANS (typically) **Cut-Through Switching**: Forward an ethernet frame as soon as we receive it rather than waiting for the whole thing like in store and forward. To know where to send a frame, switches build a MAC address table. If we have a match in the table, use it. Otherwise, we send it to everyone (*flooding*). Use a TTL field in this table. ### The need for a Spanning Tree **Problem**: In a network with redundancy, flooding can cause cycles! - **Solution**: Build a spanning tree between nodes, frames can only be forwarded between nodes with an edge. #### Algorithm A distributed algorithm where all switches (nodes) in the network must elect a root. *The root is defined as the switch with the smallest identifier.* ##### TODO: Missing Notes
